title: Proactive Context Swap — personal brainlog
content:
Quick brainlog for a small product experiment: proactive context swap.

Why: users sometimes want the assistant to change tack mid-conversation when the topic drifts or when a new, distinct task appears. Currently we rely on explicit user prompts ("actually, now do X") or session resets. I want to explore a low-friction, reversible UX that offers to swap the live conversation context to a different context bundle without losing the original thread.

Problem statement:
- Long multi-topic chats accumulate unrelated state (background facts, goals, instructions) that bias generation and make follow-up tasks noisy.
- Users frequently open a side-task and then want to return to the original flow but can't easily isolate which memory/priming to keep.
- Explicit context management is powerful but heavy; a lightweight suggestion flow could reduce friction.

High-level idea:
- Detect when the conversation intent has shifted (signal heuristics below).
- Offer a non-modal in-line affordance: "Switch to focused task mode: Draft email about X (preserve current chat)" with two quick actions: "Switch" and "Keep both as tabs" or "No thanks".
- When switched, the model uses a separate context bundle (KV cache + prompt prefix); the old thread is frozen and accessible via a small tab/peek UI.
- Provide an automatic easy rollback for first N turns (undo/swap-back).

Signals to detect intent/topic shift (initial heuristics):
- Sudden change in topical embedding distance between incoming user messages and rolling window (last 6 messages).
- Presence of explicit task markers "write", "draft", "summarize", "todo" plus named entities indicating new target (e.g., email, jira).
- User uses imperative single-turn requests after a long context: likely side-task.
- Latency pattern change: longer generation time with higher repetition could mean the model is struggling with cross-topic memory contamination.

UX options (low to high friction):
1) Passive suggestion chip: show small gray chip below response: "This looks like a new task—try focused mode". Tap to open modal with two choices.
2) Inline toggle: ephemeral banner with "Switch context / Keep current".
3) Explicit tab structure: conversations become tabs automatically labeled by inferred topic; heavier but powerful for pro users.

Data model changes/requirements:
- Context bundle concept (prototype): reference prompt + lightweight KV snapshots + last-turn cache. Each bundle gets an ID and small metadata (title, creation time, source turns).
- Ability to checkpoint snapshots cheaply and retrieve by ID.
- Storage considerations: ephemeral by default (30 days) unless user pins.
- Rollback window tracked by request IDs so we can revert routing to previous bundle.

Privacy/permissions:
- When turning on for hosted API customers, ensure user-visible doc that explains snapshots and retention.
- For private/dedicated customers, expose config to disable auto-snapshot or control retention.

User flows / example stories:
- Product manager asks the assistant to draft a release note in the middle of debugging an incident thread. Suggestion chip appears; they tap "Switch". Assistant drafts in focused context (no incident noise). After finishing, they hit "Return to incident" and the original thread is restored exactly.
- Developer asks for code review, then asks for test plan — system suggests creating a separate context for the test plan. The two are kept as lightweight tabs named "Code review" and "Test plan".

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Heuristic detection triggers suggestion in >= 70% of meaningful intent switches in a 50-user pilot.
- Users can switch and undo within 10 turns without loss of previous content.
- No significant increase in average token cost per conversation beyond storage of small snapshot metadata.

Metrics to track:
- Suggestion acceptance rate (taps / offers).
- Time-to-first-action after suggestion appears.
- Fraction of switched contexts that are pinned or lead to >1 follow-up actions.
- Rollback rate (how often users revert to previous bundle).
- QA signals: any increase in hallucination/regression measured by micro-evals on switched flows.

Risks & unknowns:
- Over-suggesting will annoy users; need to tune precision.
- Edge cases where topic shift is subtle and the suggestion removes helpful context.
- Complexity for developers if bundles multiply; need a compact list UI.

Implementation sketch (engineering notes):
- Prototype purely client-side: create a UI-only toggle that instructs the server to attach or detach an additional prompt prefix and a minimal separate KV cache ID. This enables testing without heavy storage changes.
- Backend: lightweight snapshot store (metadata + pointer to serialized prefix + small KV shard). TTL default 30 days.
- Routing change: requests carry optional bundle_id to target a specific context. Default behavior unchanged.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What threshold for embedding distance should trigger suggestion? (A/B test 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7)
- Should the suggestion be client-only (no server change) for first experiment? Pros: faster iteration. Cons: model still influenced by full history unless we actually route.
- Pinning UX: how many pinned bundles before we force manual cleanup?
- Analogs: check "note-taking app" mental model vs "inbox with tabs". Which is simpler for least-technical users?

Next steps:
1) Draft short prototype spec for engineering (one-pager + API extension sketch).
2) Quick client-only prototype (Chrome extension / Console-only) to test acceptance.
3) Run a 50-user pilot with developers and internal teams for two weeks.
4) Collect metrics, iterate heuristics.

Scratch ideas (random):
- Auto-title bundles based on top-3 nouns and verb, e.g., "Draft: release note". Allow user overwrite.
- Provide a "sandbox run" where the assistant shows a diff of how answers change if you switch contexts before committing. Might help trust.
- Lightweight keyboard shortcut to "pause & snapshot" for power users.

Notes to self: keep the initial scope tiny. Aim for suggestion chips + client-side bundle tag + server-side mapping for rollback. Avoid heavy UI like tabs in MVP.

References to look up:
- pull infra notes from GH: redwood/inference#5423 (session checkpointing mock)
- previous quick experiment notes: "session-handoff-experiments-pad" (internal drive)

Random todo list:
- [ ] Sketch UI for chip + rollback toast
- [ ] Write API extension draft (bundle_id optional param)
- [ ] Mock server changes with ephemeral in-memory snapshot store prototype
- [ ] Recruit 8 internal users for pilot

End of brainlog. Will refine into a small PRD if signals look good after pilot.
